verdict: C — Moderate DD overlay. MDD 35.9% (improved from 58.1%). CAGR 9.6% (sacrifice 28%). FF5 alpha +4.19%. No promotion — same structural issues as ddA with slightly worse risk-adjusted metrics.

gate0_pit.c5_overlay_t1: PASS — same dd_lag = c(0, dd_pct[-n_f]) as ddA
gate0_pit.c9_vt_dd_same_day: PASS — dd_lag is t-1 lag. Same code path as ddA, only DD_START/DD_FULL differ.
gate0_pit.detail: Identical PIT structure to ddA. Only parameters differ (10/25 vs 7/22). All C1-C11 PASS.

gate1_performance.detail: MDD 35.9% vs ddA 35.0% — nearly identical. CAGR 9.6% identical to ddA. But SR 0.581 < ddA 0.620 because vol is higher (16.4% vs 15.4%). The wider DD threshold lets more drawdown pass before braking, increasing vol without improving CAGR.

gate2_artifacts.files: performance.csv, hurdle_result.json, sim_result.rds, equity_curve.png, annual_returns.png, analysis_multifactor.csv

gate3_role_honesty.detail: Same issue as ddA. CAGR 9.6% cannot support core_alpha. Diversifier is honest.

gate4_statistical.detail: OOS 0.148 even weaker than ddA (0.156). Rolling positive rate 78.3% < ddA 82.6%. Moderate DD lets more OOS degradation through.

gate5_ff5.detail: FF5 alpha +4.19%/yr (t=1.014). Survival rate 63.4% — worse than ddA (68.4%). Wider DD threshold absorbs more alpha. HML -0.42 (stronger anti-value than ddA -0.38).

comparison_note: Strictly dominated by ddA: similar CAGR, similar MDD, but worse SR (0.581 vs 0.620) and worse OOS (0.148 vs 0.156). No advantage over ddA.
promotion_reason: Dominated by ddA on all key metrics. CAGR 9.6% < 16% target.
